evidence: All changes are conditional engineering hypotheses. Baseline loop coefficients are inherited scenarios; NASA evidence supports mechanisms and limitations, not the industrial recovery, cost or service-life coefficients.
assumptions: Water quality recovery applies to four already processed streams. The separate 5 kg/person/day additional makeup stays unchanged because its recoverability is not established.
Structural recovery changes from inherited net 95% to 99% collection times 99% quality. Existing full bulk/metal conversion energy remains; extra sorting and equipment are charged.
Household goods use a steady annual return approximation already implicit in the baseline; no recovered goods are added to the capital scrap bank.

Eligible active hardware is inspected at its inherited destination. Source workshops are co-located with source tugs and plants; lunar-lander workshops are at the depot. No lunar-to-source movement is implied.

A retired component becomes eligible only one year after retirement, before the existing two-year refurbishment/commissioning work period. Requalified units receive the original expected life; this is an engineering hypothesis.
Repair kit mass displaces equal old component mass. No value or recovery credit is assigned to rejects, displaced parts, or chemical exhaust.
Equipment intensities, processing energy, direct staff productivity and quality acceptance are explicit sensitivity assumptions, not demonstrated lunar industrial performance.
Seed flows are represented by the inherited eight-year average; no new executable deployment sequence is claimed.

The retained 5 kg/person/day allowance originally covered landscape/agricultural losses before explicit crop/fish balances were added. Potential overlap remains unquantified; the baseline and all primary variants retain the allowance.

A separate combined_without_residual_allowance endpoint sets only the legacy 5 kg/person/day allowance to zero. This is a 100 percent overlap or complete-capture credit ceiling, not a measured correction; explicit domestic, crop, fish and industrial water losses remain.
